clue.text: Quality, it seems, of a fragrant cape.

parts.note: fragrant means sweet-smelling, giving off a scent
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names

explanation.surface: A whimsical musing on what quality a sweet-smelling headland might possess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it seems' warns that the answer is a mock compound: a scented headland would have this quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is an abstract noun naming the property of being sweet-smelling, so it is a quality.

clue.text: Ham!

parts.note: a ham is a bad actor, and as a verb to ham is to perform with exaggerated gestures

explanation.definitionFit: To ham it up on stage is to exaggerate a performance, which is the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Out of form season for children.

parts.note: a player off their game is out of form
spring is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A remark about a time of year when children are not at their best.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's children or descendants, a direct synonym.

clue.text: What an impression the idol leaves!

definitions.text: What an impression the idol leaves!

parts.words: What an impression the idol leaves
parts.note: an impression is a likeness or picture, and an idol is a carved likeness of a god, so both senses meet in one word

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a likeness or impression and a carved idol, as in graven idols in the Bible.

clue.text: "Youth's a stuff will not —" (T Night).

parts.note: a line from Feste's song in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, ending 'Youth's a stuff will not' and then the missing word

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Feste's song 'O Mistress Mine' in Twelfth Night ends with this line.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word of the quotation means to last or persist, which youth does not.

clue.text: Busy, having got Indoors.

definitions.meaning: busy means engaged, not free, as a telephone line or a person
having taken possession of a house and moved in, as tenants of a building

explanation.definitionFit: Something taken or in use is engaged, and a house taken by tenants is inhabited.

clue.text: Run off, Billy-it's the wilderness for you

parts.note: scape is an old form of escape, to run off
a billy is a male goat

explanation.surface: Someone tells a runaway billy goat that he will be banished to the wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: In Leviticus a goat bearing the people's sins was sent out into the wilderness, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical goat that carried the people's sins was driven out into the desert, so one who takes the blame is banished.

clue.text: Exalted prelate, no longer, a little priest:

indicators.note: the prelate is no longer one when it loses its priestly element, so those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: PR is a short form, a little bit, of priest

explanation.surface: A bishop raised high is now demoted to a mere priest.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old adjective the answer means raised up in spirit, uplifted or proud.

clue.text: Loud' speaker as "early as the Trojan war!

definitions.text: Loud' speaker as "early as the Trojan war!

parts.note: a herald in Homer's account of the Trojan war whose voice was as loud as fifty men's

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek herald in the Iliad was famed for his huge voice, so a loudspeaker from ancient times.

clue.text: Tennyson's fairy country ;of faintly horns.

parts.note: a fairyland in Tennyson's song 'The splendour falls', where horns are heard faintly blowing

explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's line about horns blowing faintly from a fairy realm names this land of elves.

clue.text: Walkie-talkie' sort of-riddle ?

parts.note: a parlour game in which players act out syllables of a word, walking and talking, for others to guess

explanation.definitionFit: The parlour game is a riddle acted out in scenes, with movement and sometimes speech.

clue.text: Red-cap in the: drink. Is liberal.

indicators.note: the military police sit inside the drink, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer
a redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the red cap band; MP is military police

explanation.surface: A soldier has a drink and is generous with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping, which matches the answer.

clue.text: Exhibit? Give again.

definitions.meaning: to exhibit is to show or portray something
to present something a second time, read as re- plus present

explanation.definitionFit: To portray or depict is to show, while the hyphenated form means hand over a second time.

clue.text: I've the mixture — try a pinch.

indicators.note: a mixture is a blend, so the letters of the two words are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone offers a blend of snuff and invites a friend to try a pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinch is slang for steal.

clue.text: Even Latin would do for his address.

indicators.note: the letters would do, would serve, when they are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A suitor wonders whether a Latin phrase would suit his love letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A love card sent on 14 February is a lover's address to his sweetheart.

clue.text: Crier joe, turned merry-maker if you

indicators.note: turned means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A town crier called Joe becomes a reveller.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rejoices celebrates, and so is a reveller.

clue.text: Irate face — the 'result of the self-service?:

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are the raw material from which the jumbled result is produced

explanation.surface: An angry expression is what comes of having to serve yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant where diners carry their own food from a counter is the classic self-service eatery.

clue.text: The drag no-longer on apparently.

parts.note: to drag along behind is to trail, and something no longer on is off, so a phrase meaning to fade away

explanation.definitionFit: A voice or effort that fades gradually into silence is said to trail away, dwindling.

clue.text: Good patrons locally might one say?

definitions.text: Good patrons locally might one say?

parts.note: the faithful customers of a local pub, who come in every night

explanation.definitionFit: Frequent customers of a pub or shop are its habitual patrons.

clue.text: Uncommon little piece of Welsh origin.

parts.note: rare means uncommon
a bit is a little piece

explanation.surface: A small, unusual fragment traced back to Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, a dish named as Welsh, which is why it is of Welsh origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheese dish is always called Welsh, so the word is tied to Wales by name.

clue.text: One may have to suffocate in the dust, so

definitions.text: One may have to suffocate in the dust, so

parts.words: One may have to suffocate in the dust
parts.note: in dusty air a person may need to choke back a cough or sneeze

explanation.definitionFit: To suppress or smother something, such as a cough, is to choke it back.

clue.text: Offensive appearance of a sty ?.

parts.note: a sty is a swelling on the eyelid, making a painful eye, and an ugly sight is an offensive appearance

explanation.definitionFit: An ugly object spoiling a view is an offence to sight; a sty literally makes a painful eye.

clue.text: May be just a superficial polish.

definitions.text: May be just a superficial polish.

parts.words: May be just a superficial polish
parts.note: a thin surface layer laid over cheaper wood, or figuratively a surface show of good manners

explanation.definitionFit: A thin decorative surface layer, and by extension a surface show hiding what lies beneath.

clue.text: Like one with a good grasp of things.

definitions.text: Like one with a good grasp of things.

parts.words: Like one with a good grasp of things
parts.note: having a firm hold, whether physically gripping or keeping facts in the memory

explanation.definitionFit: Describes a memory or grip that holds on well, keeping what it takes in.

clue.text: It indicates the time of action

definitions.text: It indicates the time of action

parts.words: It indicates the time of action
parts.note: in grammar a verb form shows whether an action is past, present or future

explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the verb form marking past, present or future is its time reference.

clue.text: Quite right to have a.dip here.

definitions.text: Quite right to have a.dip here.

parts.words: Quite right to have a.dip here
parts.note: the spa city of Bath in Somerset, famous for Roman baths, is just the place for a swim

explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English spa city in Somerset with Roman baths, so taking a dip there is fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a dip is to swim or wash in water.

clue.text: They are often up in arms.

definitions.text: They are often up in arms.

parts.words: They are often up in arms
parts.note: not angry people but infants carried in someone's arms

explanation.definitionFit: Infants too young to walk are carried, hence the phrase about those in arms.

clue.text: Hold-up? That's nothing, grab me back!

indicators.note: back says the two words are read from the end to the start

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A robbery victim invites the robber to seize them in return.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade halts shipments, a stoppage or delay.

clue.text: Yes, you may -come to taste free' -this.

definitions.text: Yes, you may -come to taste free' -this.

parts.words: Yes, you may -come to taste free' -this
parts.note: a system of free public services where anyone can come and receive benefits without paying

explanation.definitionFit: Britain's post-war system of free health care and benefits gives services to all at no charge.
